correctness.rationale: For the stated characteristic-two problem the three pair partitions and their nine choices of slopes give all 27 lines of the smooth cubic. A point of weight two in P³(F_4) lies on three lines of one partition; a point of weight four lies on one line of each partition. There are 6·3+3³=45 such points, all intersections are defined over F_4, and the three directions at each are distinct on the smooth surface. For each partition the lines are connected via the weight-two points, and the slope-one lines of the three partitions meet. Thus the ordinary planar triples have total δ=135 and the connected normalization calculation gives p_a=109. At a triple, products of two branch equations generate order-two jets on the third branch, so the conductor kills jets of order at least two. The constant gluing quotient has torus rank two locally; the residual defect of the three linear coefficients modulo the two-dimensional space of ambient differentials is one-dimensional and additive. These defects descend as vector spaces and together give G_a^45. Normalization has no positive-genus component. The directed incidence graph yields the torus character cycle lattice of rank 64. The independent graph replay gives trace 0 and mod-two rank(F−1)=32, forcing 32 regular summands by the integral involution classification; an alternative argument via an invariant spanning tree gives the same integral conclusion directly. Even m fixes the whole graph. Surjectivity on k-points follows from Lang for U, and the 2-primary kernel and odd-order torus group split abstractly by primary decomposition. The contextual rank-91 comparison is correct for the smooth odd-characteristic Fermat cubic (p>3); it cannot be extended to p=3, where the cubic equation is a cube. The Finding's stated field of application is characteristic two only.
residual_risks: The in-scope characteristic-two theorem is correct. Any separate use of the rank-91 contrast should explicitly exclude characteristic three.

evidence: On the explicit binary lines fixed by squaring, both slopes must be 1. The point with all coordinates 1 joins the three lines; each remaining fixed point has two nonzero coordinates and belongs to just one fixed line. Thus all fixed edges are in one tree.

Start with that fixed tree and add the pair of lifts of each rooted quotient-tree edge leading to a free vertex pair. This adds one edge per new vertex, so introduces no cycles. In the invariant spanning tree's fundamental-cycle basis Frobenius permutes each pair of non-tree edges with the given orientation, with no fixed edge outside the tree. This gives Z[C_2]^32 without a new integral lattice calculation.

The ordinary triple-point unit defect is the standard first-jet calculation (only order-one terms survive); the abelian quotient is zero by rational normalization. Lang and primary decomposition give the finite groups once these data are known. In fact for q even the two integers q−1 and q+1 are coprime, so the finite abelian torus group does not distinguish a split/norm-one pair from an induced pair even though the algebraic tori differ.

originality.rationale: The binary-complement record alone supplies the exact incidence geometry but only rational Frobenius information. The distinct indexed prime-degree Fermat Picard-torus record additionally supplies, in Proof §§2–4, the same normalization-to-cycle identification and a characteristic-independent equivariant spanning-tree argument for a connected fixed subgraph and free remaining orbits. Apply that proof to the already-described binary configuration: the three fixed slope-one lines all meet at [1:1:1:1] and each has two weight-two rational points whose supports are its coordinate pairs. Those six two-element supports are distinct. The fixed graph is therefore a connected tree on 10 vertices and 9 edges. The spanning-tree argument applies with no fixed edge deleted, and all 64 non-tree edges pair up, giving exactly the claimed 32 regular integral summands. This is coverage by the scope of the proved method combined with the explicit same-object geometry, not a literal p=2 substitution into the other record's stated theorem or an inference of priority from the date.
residual_risks: The bounded primary search did not establish historical priority. The FAIL is a demonstrable mathematical implication of inspected sources, not attribution of temporal order between the same-day records or a conclusion from a weak search.

value.rationale: The object and integral torus invariant are natural; a rational character alone really is insufficient to recover the algebraic torus. For this known graph, however, the inspected integral orbit-tree proof and the explicit fixed lines already determine the claimed lattice mechanically. The remaining vector/additive part is an ordinary first-jet normalization calculation, and the rational point groups follow formally. The record supplies correct verification and a useful corollary, but no distinct non-mechanically-implied invariant to retain under the stated criterion.
residual_risks: This assessment does not negate the value of integral torus classifications for other fixed-graph patterns, or assign precedence between contemporaneous records.
